title: State & Backends
summary: What the state file is and why Terraform needs it, drift and refresh, remote backends (S3 with native lockfile locking, HCP Terraform), state locking and secrets, and every tool for changing state safely: state commands, import/moved/removed blocks, -refresh-only and -replace.
objectives: Explain what state stores, why Terraform needs it, and read a state file
Detect drift with refresh and choose between reverting it and accepting it with `-refresh-only`
Configure an S3 backend with `use_lockfile`, encryption and versioning, and migrate state to it
Explain state locking and recover from a stale lock with `force-unlock`
Refactor safely with `moved` blocks and `terraform state mv`, and stop managing objects with `removed` blocks
Bring existing infrastructure under management with `import` blocks and `-generate-config-out`
Recover from common state mistakes using backups, bucket versioning and `terraform state push`
